topPRs.title: DO NOT MERGE: combined measurement branch for the lokahi interop suites
topPRs.author: claude
topPRs.body:
<!-- ccr-slack-attribution -->
_Requested by **Sebastian Stammler** · [Slack thread](https://oplabs-pbc.slack.com/archives/C0BHEH8TG91/p1787240090382769)_

**DO NOT MERGE.** This is a temporary measurement branch. It exists only so CI will run the interop acceptance suites against lokahi with three in-flight changes stacked together, and it will be closed as soon as the numbers are recorded. Nothing here is intended for review or merge, and the acceptance job is expected to be red -- that red is the measurement.

Part of #22546.

## What is on this branch

#22620's head, with two open PRs merged into it and the acceptance variant flipped to `supernode_kind: lokahi`:

| | head measured |
| --- | --- |
| #22620 (base of this branch) | `c06d92d4f8146a5c517ec749a79b52cd3d74a114` |
| #22626 -- safe-head lower bound re-read each round instead of latched at cold start | `5c3b717231a7144549e05986aff00214cd6eb920` |
| #22628 -- chain RPCs served on one socket, routed by chain | `e6c4738715b5b27691168f5de899d5f5e80710d4` |
| #22631 -- op-test-sequencer teardown panic, nil ensemble handed to a deferred `Close` | `4bacec0182dbd079fa5d2163d0742f171186f2d1` |

Every merged head was re-resolved from the API immediately before merging, because each had moved from the SHA originally quoted.

`scoped-commits subject check` is expected to fail on this branch and should be ignored: it lints commit-message subjects, and the commits here are merge commits on a branch that exists to be thrown away. Fixing it would mean rewriting history for no gain. `rust-clippy` and `rust-tests` are the checks that matter -- they are the verdict on the merge resolution below -- and `memory-all-kona-lokahi-op-reth-fusaka` is also expected red, because lokahi does not pass the suites yet; its contents are the deliverable, not its colour.

## The merge conflict, and how it was resolved

#22626 and #22628 conflict in `rust/lokahi/src/supernode.rs`. #22626 changes `Supernode.chains` to `Box<[OpenChain]>` -- its new post-`Chain::load` phase, which carries the safe-head database -- while #22628 keeps `Box<[Chain]>` and rewrites the neighbouring `admin_rpc` doc comment for the single socket.

Resolved by taking #22626's `OpenChain` field type together with #22628's single-socket doc comment. They are different concerns on adjacent lines, so both intents survive. `struct Chain` and `struct OpenChain` both remaining is deliberate on #22626's part: `Chain` is the configured phase, `OpenChain` the opened one.

The conflict is larger than the field type alone. `compose` gained an `rpc: Option<&SupernodeRpc>` parameter on #22628 while #22626 moved `compose` from `impl Chain` onto `impl OpenChain`, so the parameter had to move with it. In the merged tree `compose` sits on `impl OpenChain` (`supernode.rs:422`), takes the `rpc` parameter, and is called at `:282` as `.compose(&l1, &l1_chain_config, rpc.as_ref())`.

The failure mode that would have compiled is keeping #22626's body and signature but never threading `rpc` through, or losing `safe_db`. Both were checked by reading, because a dropped safe-head database does not fail to compile -- it surfaces later as `NotEnabled` to `HistoryUnavailable`, which prints the *same* halt string as pruned records (`lokahi/src/interop/chain.rs:133`), so it would inflate the very number this branch exists to measure. In the merged tree:

- `rpc` reaches the per-chain RPC construction at `:485` (`rpc.map(|rpc| rpc_builder(&settings, rpc.addr()))`) and the chain-routed launcher at `:493-494` (`rpc.map(|rpc| rpc.launcher(settings.l2_chain_id))` into `with_rpc_launcher`).
- `safe_db` reaches the chain controller at `:489` (`.with_safe_db(safe_db)`), on the same builder chain as `with_dependency_set` and `with_external_cross_safe`.
- The destructure is `OpenChain`'s five-field pattern, not `Chain`'s three.
- `Chain::load` stays pure and `.open()` stays the last step, after every check: load at `:141`, activation at `:146`, both `bail!`s at `:161` and `:177`, `.open()` only at `:195`. A rejected chain set still leaves no rocksdb LOCK behind.
- `admin::serve` is gone and `admin::module` is used with `rpc.set_root(...)` at `:257`; `rpc_socket` is absent repo-wide. #22626 touches none of those, so they land cleanly.

**The build was never run locally.** Disk in the container stayed between 200 MB and 1 GB throughout and a lokahi build needs roughly 2.6 GB, so `rust-clippy` and `rust-tests` on this branch are the first compile of this tree. If they fail, the resolution is wrong and the acceptance numbers from this run are void.

The conflict is a real one that will recur when these two PRs are restacked for real, independently of this branch.

## What is being measured

Pass / fail / skip and the total record count from `memory-all-kona-lokahi-op-reth-fusaka`, against these baselines:

- op-supernode control: 768 passed, 0 failed, 25 skipped, **793 records**
- lokahi, first measured run: 202 / 138 / 25 on 365 records
- lokahi, with the interop activation override: 190 / 130 / 25 on 345 records

#22631 is in the merge specifically to protect the record count: without it the nil-receiver teardown panic kills whole test binaries and takes their results with them, which is how an earlier run reported only 345 of 793. A pass/fail split measured on a third of the suite cannot be compared to anything.

The record count matters as much as the pass count: a large shortfall against 793 means test binaries died and took their results with them, so a lower failure count can mean less evidence rather than more passing. The specific question is whether the 79 tests that halted on `which L1 block made timestamp N safe is no longer recorded on this node` clear, which is what #22626 predicts.

topPRs.title: kona-engine: mirror op-node sync regimes to fix the sync-tester verifier livelock
topPRs.author: claude
topPRs.body:
<!-- ccr-slack-attribution -->
_Requested by **Sebastian Stammler** · [Slack thread](https://oplabs-pbc.slack.com/archives/C0BHEH8TG91/p1787240090382769)_

Fixes the livelock behind all five failing `sync_tester` acceptance tests (`op-acceptance-tests/tests/supernode/sync_tester/`) by mirroring op-node's behaviour, per the governing rule for lokahi. Part of #22537.

## Before

All five tests timed out at ~720s in a single livelock, spamming >50MB of paired warnings (`sync_tester.go:185` "Requested block is ahead of sync tester state" / kona "Failed to fetch unsafe l2 block for consolidation") at ~5k attempts/s:

1. Kona adopted gossiped tips the EL answered SYNCING for regardless of sync phase (`insert/task.rs`, `synchronize/task.rs:94-98`), so the unsafe head named blocks the EL could not serve.
2. Consolidation's fetch of such a block surfaced as `FailedToFetchUnsafeL2Block` → **Temporary** (`consolidate/error.rs`), retried forever with no realignment and no pacing (`tasks/task.rs` retried with only a `yield_now`).
3. On a cold restart, nothing ever put a forkchoice update on the wire until gossip did, so against a reset sync-tester session (CLSync, sequencer far ahead) EL sync never "finished" and derivation never started at all.

## After — per gap, with the op-node behaviour being mirrored

**G1 — consolidation fetch miss → op-node's stall/reset split** (`kona-engine`, commit 1)
- Rust: `consolidate/task.rs` + `consolidate/error.rs`: a miss is now `AwaitingELSyncUnsafeL2Block` (Temporary) while `!el_sync_finished`, and `MissingUnsafeL2Block` (Reset — walkback realigns the unsafe head, then the gate flips to force-building) after. Not-found-shaped RPC error responses fold into the miss.
- Go: `op-node/rollup/attributes/attributes.go:204-221` (NotFound → EL-sync stall vs `rollup.ResetEvent`), `:222-227` (other errors Temporary), `:185-193` (post-reset force-build gate), `op-service/eth/errors.go:10-27` (`MaybeAsNotFoundErr` hardening). The string set is a documented **superset** of op-node's (bare `"not found"` included): kona adopts optimistic heads and so fetches ahead of the EL where op-node's payload queue never would, and the sync tester answers that miss with a bare `not found` error (`sync_tester.go:183-187`).

**G2 — REVISED after CI (commit 2 shipped a gate, commit 6 removed it): the gossip EL-sync channel stays open past the initial sync**
- The first version refused SYNCING unsafe heads once `el_sync_finished` was set, mirroring op-node's CL-sync regime. CI proved that wrong for kona: op-node's CL-sync mode has reqresp sync and an unsafe payload queue to catch up with; kona has neither, so adopting the gossiped tip and pointing the EL at it is its *only* unsafe-chain catch-up channel — and a verifier that falls behind (restart, dropped peer) re-enters it after the initial sync. The gate stranded such verifiers forever: `rust-e2e-restart` `TestSequencerRestart`, `rust-e2e-simple-kona` `TestSyncUnsafeBecomesSafe`, and the 7 kona CL-sync acceptance tests (`TestUnsafeChainNotStalling_*`, `TestCLELDivergence`, `TestGlamsterdamP2PUnsafeBlockBecomesSafe`) all failed on the new drop log.
- Final behaviour: op-node's EL-sync regime in both phases (`engine_controller.go:587-594`, `sync_deriver.go:102-115`) — unchanged from develop. The sync-tester livelock is instead broken where op-node breaks it: at G1's consolidation fetch-miss reset, which realigns the unsafe head with the EL and flips the gate to force-building (`attributes.go:185-193, 204-221`).

**G3 — paced temporary retries** (`kona-engine`, commit 3)
- Rust: `tasks/task.rs`: exponential backoff (100ms base, 10s cap) instead of a bare `yield_now` in the Temporary retry loop.
- Go: `op-node/rollup/driver/step_scheduling_deriver.go:97-109` + `op-service/retry/strategies.go:49-55` (`retry.Exponential()`, capped at 10s).

**Startup — op-node's initial reset** (`kona-node-service` + `kona-engine`, commit 4)
- Rust: `chain_controller/controller.rs`: the controller's first step runs the walkback reset — but only against an EL that reports a **finalized block**, op-node's own EL-sync discriminator ("the engine has no finalized block until its initial snap-sync completes", `engine_controller.go:597-624`; EL sync is only entered "if there is no finalized block", `:29`). A fresh EL (no finalized label — every real EL in the short-lived e2e/acceptance suites, where nothing finalizes) is left to the gossip bootstrap exactly as on develop; the sync-tester EL always serves its finalized label, so the probe runs there, derivation starts at once, and the cold-restart CLSync deadlock is gone. The probe's FCU doubles as the EL-sync marker (VALID → derivation starts; SYNCING → bootstrap unchanged), and a walkback the EL cannot serve falls back to the gossip bootstrap rather than failing startup. `task_queue/core.rs`: `Engine::reset` now retries RPC-level walkback failures with backoff instead of returning them — which previously killed the requesting actor (and the node) when the EL was merely unavailable at startup (`ResetForkchoiceError("An RPC error occurred: client error (SendRequest)")`, the `startup_resync` `ConnectsAfterELUnavailableAtStartup` failure).
- Go: `op-node/rollup/derive/pipeline.go:181-190, 224` (`initialReset` at startup in every sync mode), `op-node/rollup/engine/engine_controller.go:1423-1432` (reset request → `FindL2Heads` walkback; a failure re-emits the reset event rather than dying), `op-node/rollup/driver/sync_deriver.go:225-230`.

Note: the devstack deliberately passes no sync mode to lokahi (`op-devstack/sysgo/multichain_supernode_runtime.go:711-714`), so kona keeps its modeless design. The regime selection is now behavioural rather than keyed on `el_sync_finished`: an EL with no finalized block gets the gossip EL-sync bootstrap (op-node's EL-sync mode), one with chain state gets the startup walkback probe (op-node's startup `initialReset`), and either way the unsafe-gossip channel stays open — a non-syncing EL (the sync tester's CL-sync sessions) converges through consolidation-miss resets plus derivation force-builds instead of livelocking. Expected trade: against such an EL the node performs a walkback reset per missed-gossip stretch (bounded by the paced retries and cheap re-derivation from the last safe head) — the honest cost of modelessness; an explicit sync-mode flag remains the follow-up if that churn matters in practice.

## Round 2: the receipts wedge (after the fixes above)

With the engine-layer fixes in, CI (job 5518771) showed the old livelock and reset churn gone and derivation healthy — but all five tests still timed out on their first `CheckAll`, because **interop verification could not parse the sync-tester's receipts**, so cross-safe never left 0 (and with interop active, the DSL-visible safe/finalized heads only move on cross-safe promotions):

- The sync tester served `eth_getBlockReceipts` by round-tripping the upstream EL's response through geth's consensus `types.Receipt` (`op-sync-tester/synctester/frontend/eth.go:34-35` via `backend/el_reader.go:72-73`), a type with no `from`/`to` fields — silently stripping fields the execution-apis spec requires and every real EL serves.
- alloy's `TransactionReceipt` requires `from` (alloy-rpc-types-eth-1.8.3 `receipt.rs:64`), so lokahi's verifier failed deserialization on the first block's receipts, the error classified transient (`rust/lokahi/src/interop/chain.rs` → `ChainError::Unreachable`), retried every ~2s for the full 720s budget.
- The Go stack never noticed: op-node/op-supervisor decode receipts into the same lossy geth type (`op-service/sources/receipts_rpc.go:96`), which is why the op-node twins of these tests pass against the same sync-tester EL in the same job.

Two commits:

1. **`op-sync-tester`: raw receipts passthrough** (primary) — `eth_getBlockReceipts` now relays the raw payload from the read-only EL, exactly like the existing `GetBlockByNumberJSON`/`GetBlockByHashJSON` accessors; the session ahead-of-state gate reads only `blockNumber` out of the raw JSON. The regression test pins that `from`/`to` survive through both the backend and the RPC frontend. This makes the harness faithful to real ELs for every client.
2. **`lokahi`: lenient receipt read in the verifier** (hardening) — `block_logs` only consumes logs, so it now fetches `eth_getBlockReceipts` into a logs-only local type instead of alloy's full typed receipt. This mirrors the Go stack's posture (op-geth's `Receipt` has no `from` at all): a receipt shape the Go verifier accepts must not wedge this one. The unit test deserializes the CI-captured geth-shaped receipt (no `from`) and extracts its logs.

## Round 3: two more harness-vs-spec and mirroring gaps (after the receipts fix)

With the receipts fix in (job 5519251), `AdvancesViaSyncTester` passes; the four remaining failures split into two root causes:

**Activation pair — Lagoon upgrade-gas strip asymmetry (`kona-protocol`).** Both attribute builders add only the NUT bundle's gas to a single-chain Interop activation block (kona `stateful.rs` `upgrade_gas_for_activation(false)`; op-node `interop_activation_transactions.go:37-61`), but kona's `to_system_config` stripped the *multi-chain* amount (bundle + 150k setFeature/ETHLiquidity wrappers) back out — reconstructing a gas limit 150k below the real one, so every attribute set built from the activation block onward was rejected with `-38003 gaslimit mismatch: attr=59850000, header=60000000` and the build task retried at the queue head forever. op-node strips `UpgradeGas(forks.Lagoon)` = bundle-only (`payload_util.go:62-80`, `upgrade_transaction.go:158-168`); kona now does the same. Fail-first test round-trips a single-chain activation block back to the steady-state limit.

**FromCold pair — sync-tester `engine_getPayload` responses were not spec-shaped (`op-sync-tester`).** The tester served its stored `eth.ExecutionPayloadEnvelope` (gossip shape: executionPayload + parentBeaconBlockRoot only) from every getPayload version. The spec requires `blockValue` (V2+), `blobsBundle`/`shouldOverrideBuilder`/`parentBeaconBlockRoot` (V3+), `executionRequests` (V4+); Go clients decode into the same lossy type and never noticed, but kona (getPayloadV5 → `OpExecutionPayloadEnvelopeV4`) hard-fails on the missing `blockValue` — so after a cold restart (session reset to Latest:0, every block force-built) sealing block 1 retried forever and nothing ever advanced. Same class as the receipts bug; same style of fix: the RPC frontend now wraps the stored envelope into the per-version spec response (blockValue 0, empty-but-present blobs bundle, empty executionRequests), payload untouched, Go clients unaffected. The `requested=62` / `BlockRetrievalFailed` spam was a symptom: the interop verifier's persisted DB polling a pre-restart block until the chain catches up. Fail-first frontend test pins the per-version field sets and non-null arrays.

Round-3 verification: `cargo nextest -p kona-protocol` (256) and `-p kona-derive` (206) green including the new round-trip tests; `go test ./op-sync-tester/...` green including the new getPayload shape test; clippy/fmt clean on the touched crates.

## Verification

- Round 2: `go test ./op-sync-tester/...` green (incl. the new from/to passthrough regression test); `cargo nextest -p lokahi` green (incl. the captured-receipt leniency test).
- Fail-first unit tests in every touched area: consolidate miss split and not-found mapping (bare `"not found"` included), SYNCING FCU/insert adoption in both EL-sync phases (pinning the catch-up channel the CI regression removed), temporary-retry backoff timing, `Engine::reset` walkback retry, controller startup probe (probe, finalized-gated skip, and walkback-failure fallback).
- `cargo nextest run -p kona-engine -p kona-node-service -p lokahi`: 391 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p kona-engine -p kona-node-service -p lokahi -p kona-node --all-features --all-targets`: clean.
- Nightly `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean. Docs lint (rustdoc `-D warnings`) for the touched crates: clean.
- Not run here (please run in CI / locally): the `sync_tester` acceptance suite itself — building its full dependency set exceeded this environment's disk budget.
- Repo review agents (`rust-code-reviewer`): not run — this worker session cannot spawn the repo's review agents; flagged per the contribution guide instead of skipping silently.

topPRs.title: kona-engine: local/cross-safe vocabulary and a single cross-safe promotion entry point
topPRs.author: claude
topPRs.body:
_Requested by **Sebastian Stammler** · [Slack thread](https://oplabs-pbc.slack.com/archives/C0BHEH8TG91/p1787240090382769)_

Part of #22525. Stacked on #22519.

**Before.** One head called `safe_head`, written from four places: payload insert, both consolidation paths, and the reset start-point. Under interop that head has to mean two things at once — locally derived, and cross-chain verified — and nothing in the types said which.

**After.** Two heads. `local_safe_head` is what derivation advances; `cross_safe_head` is the forkchoice `safeBlockHash`. `EngineSyncStateUpdate` has no cross-safe field, so the four old writers cannot express a cross-safe move at all — they are local-safe-only. Wire names are unchanged: `safe_l2`, the `safe` metric label, `subscribe_safe_head`.

**How.** Moving the cross-safe head requires a `CrossSafePromotion`, which has no public constructor. Outside `kona-engine` one can only be minted by the engine's `CrossSafePromoter`, handed out once by `Engine::with_external_cross_safe`. Standalone kona-node uses `Engine::new`, where `CrossSafeSource::LocalSafe` mints the trivial promotion inline, so a local-safe advance still reports local-safe == cross-safe in a single forkchoice call. Promotions may move backwards — that is how an interop rewind unwinds a decision — but are clamped at the finalized head. The depth-1 lockstep confirmation to the derivation actor now carries local-safe; driving it from cross-safe would deadlock under interop, since the promotion it would wait on itself waits on every chain's derivation.

**Review fixes.** Three behavioural changes landed after review, each with a regression test. A finality signal for a block that is not yet cross-safe is now dropped with a `warn!` rather than failing `Critical` and killing the engine actor — a routine interop state, so the producer-side fix is tracked separately in #22582. Cross-safe promotion is clamped at `local_safe_head` above as well as `finalized_head` below, warning on each, so it can no longer send `safeBlockHash` past `headBlockHash`. And initial-forkchoice emission is tracked by an explicit `forkchoice_emitted` flag instead of comparing the sync state against `Default`, which never fired for an externally promoted engine.

New tests hold cross-safe behind local-safe by withholding promotion and assert the resulting FCU labels and sync-status fields, plus the backward-promotion clamp and the standalone single-FCU path.

topPRs.title: lokahi: fix the three fixable safe-progression causes (pre-activation cross-safe, cold-start pin, L1 epoch poll cadence)
topPRs.author: claude
topPRs.body:
<!-- ccr-slack-attribution -->
_Requested by **Sebastian Stammler** · [Slack thread](https://oplabs-pbc.slack.com/archives/C0BHEH8TG91/p1787240090382769)_

Fixes the three fixable causes of the "safe progression never starts" family in the lokahi supernode acceptance matrix (diagnosed against job 5518771, lokahi, vs control 5518494, op-supernode — byte-identical op-node/op-supernode trees). All six affected tests share the surface signature "SafeL2/Finalized pinned at genesis while unsafe grows"; none is a derivation failure — what never moved was the cross-safe head, and finality behind it. Part of #22537.

Governing rule throughout: mirror op-supernode/op-node behaviour.

## A1 — pre-activation cross-safe/finalized pinning (b324572)

**Before:** lokahi's engines run `CrossSafeSource::Promoted`, and `InteropActor::promote` minted promotions only from committed verified frontiers. Pre-activation the verifier has committed nothing, so cross-safe sat at genesis for hours-away activations, and kona's `FinalizeTask` — which drops finality signals for blocks not yet cross-safe — pinned finalized with it. Evidence: `TestPreNoInbox`/`_PreActivation` polled `safe target=1 current=0` for their full budgets; `TestFinalizedL2DoesNotRegressAcrossActivation`'s log shows `Dropping a finality signal for a block that is not yet cross-safe … cross_safe=0` while L1 finality had arrived. All three pass in the Go control.

**After:** `promote()` mirrors op-node's `SafeL2Head` branches (`engine_controller.go:219-241`, `super_authority.go:23-41`): pre-activation → cross-safe follows local-safe; active-but-unverified → anchor at the canonical block at `activation-1`, clamped to genesis and bounded by local-safe; verified → unchanged. Finalization unblocks through the existing `FinalizeTask` gate. Unit tests drive the actor over a stub engine: written fail-first, 3/4 fail against the old `promote()`, all pass after.

## A2 — SafeHeadProgression cold-start window (e799f48)

**Diagnosis partially refuted on this branch.** The report's mechanism — cold start blocked on a safe-DB first-entry *stability freeze* (`current_l1` strictly past the first entry's L1 key) — exists only on the measure branch the failing job ran (`bb91ffaa99`, not an ancestor here). On this branch `first_safe_head_timestamp` needs only the first entry to exist, and the chain controller already seeds it (L2 genesis at L1 block 0, `seed_genesis_safe_head`) at its first engine reset, seconds into startup — the report's own alternative fix. What ships is a regression test pinning that property: a chain whose safe-DB holds exactly the genesis seed, behind engine query channels nothing answers, must answer `first_safe_head_timestamp` immediately. Re-introducing any wait beyond the first entry re-opens the cold-start window `TestSupernodeInterop_SafeHeadProgression`'s startup pause scan races (a cold-starting verifier answers `superroot_atTimestamp` from the handoff branch and the scan overshoots the pause point).

## A3 — kona polls L1 finality every 60s; op-node every 2s (aeb83b1)

**Before:** kona's finalized stream polled on a hardcoded `FINALIZED_STREAM_POLL_INTERVAL = 60`; op-node paces the same polls with `--l1.epoch-poll-interval`, which the devstack sets to 2s for every op-node (`multichain_supernode_runtime.go:629,766`). Devnet L1 finality starts ~126s in; lokahi's 0/60/120/180s grid first sees it at ~180s > the 150s `AwaitFinalizationAdvanced` budget — both SuperRootMigrator tests died at 153.8s/153.7s in both lokahi jobs (a hard timeout, not a race), and `finreg.log`'s only finality signal lands at genesis+180.9s, exactly poll #3.

**After:** `L1Config::l1_epoch_poll_interval`, default unchanged at 60s, exposed as kona-node's `--l1.epoch-poll-interval` (mirroring op-node's flag) and as `epoch-poll-interval` in lokahi's `[l1]` table; the devstack writes 2 into the generated lokahi config — the same cadence it hands op-node. Go rendering test written fail-first (fails without the devstack change), plus a lokahi TOML round-trip test.

## Deliberately excluded

Family B (`TestSupernodeLightSequencerInteropInvalidMessageReplacement`) is excluded pending a maintainer decision: the honest behaviour deadlocks by the unsafe-ingestion gate's design until finality, and the Go pass is masked by the acknowledged, unfixed op-supernode VN-resurrection bug documented in #21992 — "mirror op-supernode" there means mirroring a bug.

## Verification

- `cargo nextest run -p lokahi -p kona-node-service -p kona-node`: 99 + 226 tests pass (includes the new actor, cold-start, and config tests)
- `cargo clippy -p lokahi -p lokahi-interop -p kona-node-service -p kona-node --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean
- `cargo +nightly-2026-08-18 fmt --all -- --check`: clean
- `go test ./op-devstack/sysgo/ -run TestLokahiConfig`: pass (and fails without the devstack change)
- The lokahi acceptance matrix itself was not run locally (disk/CPU constrained runner); the sync-tester CI workflow is the end-to-end evidence.
- Repo review agents (`rust-code-reviewer`, `go-code-reviewer`) were not run in this automation pass — noting per CLAUDE.md rather than skipping silently.

topPRs.title: docs: add an architecture page and restructure the Protocol tab
topPRs.author: sbvegan
topPRs.body:
The Protocol tab had no single page explaining how the OP Stack works. Six pages each partially claimed the job and none finished it, so a reader who wanted the architecture had to assemble it from all of them. This started from a colleague evaluating the stack who gave up and read a competitor's docs to understand ours, then came back and said so.

Adds `op-stack/architecture` as the canonical system view and reorders the tab around it.

**What changes for readers**

- A new architecture page: the components, who runs each, one transaction walked through all of them, where trust sits, and what is permissionless versus privileged.
- `op-stack/protocol/overview` is retired and redirects to it. That page named op-geth as the execution engine after op-geth's end of support, and described a defeated proposal as being removed from the pre-Bedrock `StateCommitmentChain`.
- The learning track gains a stop, 13 to 14, with architecture at stop 2.
- Nav: "Protocol Information" becomes "How the protocol works" and keeps only conceptual pages; the 12 hardfork explainers move to their own group; Features drops from position 2 to 10 because it holds configuration choices, not protocol; `privileged-roles` moves to the top of Security.
- Several claims that had gone stale are corrected, including settlement being described as still using the attestation/MultiSig mechanism with permissionless fault proofs "well underway", and op-proposer posting to `L2OutputOracle`.

**Things you cannot see in the diff**
